questions.question: If a metal spoon and a wooden book are left on a table in a room for several hours, what can we say about their temperatures?
options: The metal spoon will be colder than the wooden book.
The wooden book will be colder than the metal spoon.
Both objects will reach the same temperature as the room.
Both objects will slowly warm up to be hotter than the room air.

questions.question: What happens to the particles in a solid metal bar when it is heated?
options: They stop moving completely.
They vibrate more quickly.
They start flowing past each other.
They gain mass and grow larger.

questions.question: When a solid or liquid is heated, how does the physical spacing between its particles change?
options: The separation of its particles increases.
The particles pack much closer together.
The separation remains exactly the same.
The particles merge into single giant particles.

questions.question: Which of the following occurs as a direct result of heating a solid or liquid?
options: It contracts and takes up less space.
It undergoes a temporary increase in mass.
It expands and takes up more space.
It becomes completely weightless.

questions.question: Under which condition will a hot mug of tea transfer thermal energy to the surrounding room at the fastest rate?
options: When the tea is only slightly warmer than the room air.
When the tea is at the exact same temperature as the room.
When the temperature difference between the tea and the air is greatest.
When the tea has been left to cool down for several hours.

questions.question: Why do some materials reach a higher temperature much faster than others when supplied with the same amount of heat energy?
options: Some materials are completely immune to temperature changes.
It is easier to increase the temperature of some materials than others.
All materials require identical energy to change temperature.
Liquid materials can never change temperature.

questions.question: If we have the same mass of water and copper at the same high temperature, why might they cause different amounts of heating to other objects?
options: Because copper has no thermal store.
Because the same amount of different materials at the same temperature can cause different amounts of heating.
Because water is a solid at room temperature and copper is a gas.
Because temperature is the only factor that determines how much thermal energy can be transferred.

questions.question: What does a higher specific heat capacity indicate about 1 kg of a substance at a given temperature?
options: It contains less energy in its thermal store.
It contains more energy in its thermal store.
It has a much lower boiling point.
Its particles have stopped moving entirely.

questions.question: In which states of matter do the particles move in completely random directions?
options: Only in gases.
Only in liquids and gases.
Only in solids.
In solids, liquids, and gases.

questions.question: Two blocks of iron are both at a temperature of 50ºC. Block A is twice the size and mass of Block B. Which block has more energy in its thermal store?
options: Block B, because it has fewer particles.
Block A, because the one with more particles has more energy.
Both have the same energy because they are at the same temperature.
Neither block has any energy in its thermal store.

questions.question: How should you position your eyes to get an accurate reading when using a glass liquid-in-glass thermometer?
options: Your eye must be level with the top of the coloured liquid.
You must look down on the thermometer from directly above.
You must look up at the thermometer from a low angle.
The position of your eye does not affect the accuracy of the scale.

questions.question: At what temperatures do pure ice melt and pure water boil under standard conditions?
options: Ice melts at 10ºC and water boils at 50ºC.
Ice melts at 0ºC and water boils at 100ºC.
Ice melts at -100ºC and water boils at 0ºC.
Ice melts at 100ºC and water boils at 0ºC.

questions.question: If you mix 1 litre of boiling water (100ºC) with 10 litres of cold water (10ºC), what can you predict about the final temperature?
options: It will be exactly 55ºC, the midway point.
It will be closer to the temperature of the cold water, because there was more of it.
It will be closer to the temperature of the boiling water, because hot water dominates.
It will instantly drop below 0ºC.

questions.question: What happens to the temperature along a thermal insulator when one end of it is heated?
options: The temperature increases extremely quickly along the insulator.
The temperature increases very slowly along the insulator.
The temperature instantly drops to absolute zero.
The temperature remains exactly at 100ºC at all points.

questions.question: Which statement describes how heat travels through a solid thermal conductor at the particle level?
options: Vibrating particles quickly cause the particles near to them to vibrate as well.
Particles travel from the hot end to the cold end in a continuous flow of matter.
Particles stop vibrating entirely, allowing heat to pass through the gaps.
Particles in a conductor do not interact with each other at all.

questions.question: Why are materials that contain trapped air exceptionally good thermal insulators?
options: Because trapped air creates a complete vacuum.
Because gases are very poor thermal conductors.
Because air molecules are packed extremely tightly.
Because air particles cannot vibrate.
